sentences.text: Rule thirty: at anchor, and aground.
You’ll use this one yourself every time you anchor up at night.
A vessel under fifty meters at anchor may show a single all-round white light, where it can best be seen.
A larger vessel shows two: an all-round white light in the fore part, and a second one at or near the stern, lower than the forward one.
And a vessel of one hundred meters or more must also light up her decks with her working lights.
So a big ship at anchor is lit up like a parking lot, on purpose.
A vessel aground shows her anchor lights, plus two all-round red lights in a vertical line.
One ball in the fore part means at anchor.
Three balls in a vertical line means aground.
Two red lights say she can’t maneuver.
The anchor lights say she isn’t moving.
Put them together, and she’s stuck on the bottom.
